Creating a story is quick, as adding a card is in Trello and adding an issue is in Linear: a story is added in the list it belongs in, right where it will sit. The Backlog and Next sprint each end with an "Add story" line at their foot, beneath their last card, or beneath their empty state when they have none. Clicking it opens a composer in its place: a blank story card, drawn as the parts draw one, whose title is a text box, focused, in the mode last picked for a story, with nothing else to fill in. Enter with the title empty adds nothing. Escape discards the composer, and whatever was typed in it, and the "Add story" line comes back; clicking away while its title is empty discards it too, and clicking away with a title typed adds the story, as Enter does, but opens no other composer. Dragged near the board's left or right edge, the board scrolls sideways, and near a column's top or bottom, that column scrolls, as dragging says. Only the Backlog and Next sprint take drops: Current sprint and Done open no gap, a story dropped on them stays where it was, and their cards can't be picked up, nor can a finding. Stories move too from a card's menu, "Move to next sprint" or "Move to backlog". Their order within Next sprint is the order they will be sent. A card's menu also has "Duplicate" and "Delete".
"Send sprint", a primary button at the right of Next sprint's heading, enabled while it holds a story, sends every story in it, in order, as though each had been written in the chat input on its mode's tab and sent, one after another, as the [PromptSending](../prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending) says: each task queues in its lane behind the one before it, in the order of the sprint, and each question runs at once. The stories go into the queue as one block, so nothing sent later comes between them, and the queue's auto-send carries them on as ever, as the [QueueList](../prompt-mode/queue-list/index.md#queue-list) says.
Each story starts a conversation of its own, as though New conversation had been pressed just before it, and so does each later step of a story's chain: a story never carries on the conversation of the story before it, nor of anything its lane ran before the sprint. New conversation, pressed before the sprint was sent, is left for the next prompt written in the chat input.
A story can't be sent on its own. The only way a story reaches work is through the sprint: a story in the Backlog waits until it is moved into Next sprint and the sprint is sent, and a story in Next sprint goes when the sprint does. Sending the sprint moves its stories into the "Current sprint" column, to the right of Next sprint, so Next sprint is empty again and stories added meanwhile go there, to be the sprint after. Current sprint and Done are columns of the board whatever they hold, never appearing, disappearing, or collapsing; while no sprint is under way Current sprint is empty and shows its empty state, as Done does before anything is done. While a sprint is current, Send sprint is disabled, its tooltip saying a sprint is already under way.
Send sprint only ever moves into Current sprint the stories it actually sent. A story with nothing to send, its title and its prompt both empty, is skipped: it stays in Next sprint, where it was, and Send sprint's result says, muted, how many it skipped and why, as "1 empty story left in Next sprint". Once a sprint is done, it can always be closed. Every story of Current sprint counts as ended once its task has ended, done, failed, cancelled, or stopped, or once its task can no longer be found, as when its record was deleted, it was never recorded, or the application quit before it was. A story whose task is missing is never shown as Queued, or as anything still to come: its card reads "Task missing", muted, in the theme's warning colour, its tooltip saying its task can't be found, and it counts as ended and not Done. A story still waiting in its lane's queue, or held for review, as the paused section says, is still to come and hasn't ended. So Close sprint shows as soon as no story of Current sprint is building, compiling, running, paused, queued, or held, and never waits on a task that can't arrive.

## Auto Start

Next sprint can start on its own: a "Start automatically" switch on Next sprint's heading, beside Send sprint, its tooltip saying the next sprint starts as soon as the current one is done. It starts off, and is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, so it is kept across reloads and restarts.
While it is on, once every story of Current sprint has ended Done, the current sprint closes by itself, as Close sprint closes it, and Next sprint, if it holds a story, is sent at once, as Send sprint sends it, with nobody having to start it; and while no sprint is current, a story added to an empty Next sprint starts it the same way. A sprint that ended with a story failed, cancelled, stopped, or with its task missing, never starts the next by itself: it waits, Close sprint offered as ever, and the switch's row says, in the theme's warning colour, why the next didn't start. Turning the switch off never stops a sprint already sent; it only keeps the next from starting by itself. Turning it on while no sprint is current and Next sprint holds a story starts Next sprint at once, as adding a story to it would, unless planning is paused.

## Saving

The stories, their order, and which section each is in are saved with the project's data, as the [ProjectData](../project-data/index.md#project-data) says, in `.suspense/planning/`, a file per story, holding its hidden anchor as a queued prompt's is, and an `order.json` listing the sections and their stories, so the plan is kept with the project and comes back as it was left. A story's steps are saved in its own file, in their order, as its steps say, never apart from it.

## Steps

A story can have steps: one or more further prompts, each a piece of the story done after the one before, as a chain's steps are. Each step has a prompt, a mode of its own, Code or Spec, starting as the story's, and a model and effort, starting as the story's, and may have attachments. A story with no steps is just its own prompt, as before; its prompt is always its first step.
An open story lists its steps beneath its prompt, in order, each a row numbered from 2, the story's own prompt being 1, with its mode pill and the first line of its prompt, opening in place to edit, as a story does. "Add step", beneath the last, adds one at the end, open and focused; several can be added one after another, Enter in an empty step's prompt adding none. Steps are reordered by dragging, as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) says, or Alt+Up and Alt+Down, and each has a remove button in its row and in its menu. The story's own prompt stays first and can't be moved among them.
A step belongs to its story and to nothing else. It is saved in the story's file, in a `steps` list of the story's hidden anchor, in its order, and saved as every change to the plan is, straight away; a story duplicated copies its steps, and one deleted deletes them. Its order is kept wherever the story goes, between sections, into a sprint, and back from Done.
Wherever the story is shown, its steps are too: its card in Planning shows how many beneath its title, muted, as "3 steps", with the list in its tooltip; the open story lists them as above; a proposal to add to it shows them, so what it would add to can be seen; and once it is sent, it is sent as a chain, its prompt first and each step after it in order, each step sent only once the one before it finishes, as the [PromptEditor](../prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor)'s chained tasks are, so the Tasks tab shows the story as one chain with its steps beneath it. A story sent can't be given more steps; its steps, sent or still to come, read as they were sent. In Current sprint, a story with steps lists its steps on its card, beneath its title, a line for each step, in order, each with its number, the first line of its prompt cut off with an ellipsis, and its own status, as a running chain's are in the Tasks tab; in Done, and in a finding started from the story, its steps are listed the same way, collapsed to its step count until it is expanded. The same steps, in the same order, are what every place shows, since every place reads them from the story's own file.
A step is only ever added to a story that exists. Adding one to a story that doesn't, as one deleted while a proposal naming it waited, or by another window, or whose file was removed from `.suspense/planning/` meanwhile, changes nothing: no story is made for it, no other story is given it, and nothing is saved. It says so in plain words where it was asked for, as "That story no longer exists, so the step wasn't added", in the theme's error colour, as the states say, with what was to be added kept, so it can be added to another story or as a new one. A step added to a story already sent is refused the same way, saying the story has been sent.

I added two paragraphs to Planning's motion section in `spec/scope/planning/index.pi`. `piton check` reports no problems, the build succeeded, and the rebuilt reference shows both paragraphs.

- **Keeping the open card in view:** if the open story's card was fully in view, the board now scrolls sideways as the side panel opens, in the same 150 ms motion, so the card stays fully in view. A card that was already partly hidden is left alone. Opening a story from outside the board (a proposal's "Added to …" link, or a palette or ribbon action) scrolls the board sideways and the card's column up or down until the card is fully in view, then highlights it. Clicking a card that is only partly in view opens it and scrolls just enough to show all of it. A card already fully in view scrolls nothing.
- **Changes above the view:** in a column scrolled away from its top, a card above the view can be added, deleted, or change height (status or step lines arriving, a sprint closing). The column's scroll then shifts by the same amount instantly, so the visible cards don't move. The thumb stays steady, linking to `Scrollbar.steadiness`. A column at its top keeps its top.

**Added by me:** the prompt said "just enough", and I made that explicit: a scroll stops with the card at the nearest edge of the view, never centred. The scroll shift for changes above the view is instant, with no animation.

**Also fixed:** a line in the existing motion text began with `style:`, which split the section under a stray "Style" heading. I reworded it, so the section is one piece again.

**Anchors for the code:** `Planning.motion` (the two new paragraphs) and `Scrollbar.steadiness`, with `Planning.layout` for how the side panel narrows the board.
